tasks.short: Explain how counseling may help a client and record the advice.

steps.what: Discuss concerns, counseling options, expectations and the client's questions
Write and check the counseling advice note

loop.input: Psychologist's brief post-session dictation of concerns, options explained, client preference and agreed next step
loop.output: Draft advice note with statements linked to dictation passages
loop.check: Psychologist checks clinical meaning, negation, client preferences and all advice against the dictation, correcting omissions before accepting
loop.stop: One draft and one correction attempt; unclear audio or invented details cause manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: The note condenses free clinical speech; a fixed form cannot faithfully summarize that narrative. Test plain dictation first.

steps.what: Commit the checked counseling note to the clinical record

tasks.design: Keep the client conversation human and first test native dictation and note templates in the clinical record category of {OTHER}. If those leave substantial editing, use a bounded draft from the psychologist's post-session dictation, then commit only the corrected version the psychologist accepts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Narrative advice notes require typing and clinical phrasing after the conversation.
tasks.enabler_now: Speech-driven draft notes are available, while record templates and dictation remain cheaper options.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining uncertain benefits and responding to distress or reluctance.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust and judge whether counseling is appropriate without promising outcomes.
tasks.altitude: A little less note writing; client advice and clinical responsibility remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: The supplied digest reports speech-driven reporting in Dutch mental health services; it does not establish savings for this task.
The supplied digest describes an ambient documentation study in a child mental health clinic; this is evidence for note drafting, not automated counseling.

assumptions: Boundary includes advice conversation and the associated clinical note. The note is not excluded merely because conversation dominates. No client letter or referral is assumed.

s1 produces the discussion. In s2 the psychologist dictates a short account; remaining time includes that new capture, complete meaning review and corrections. There is no ambient recording or free patient capture transfer.

Dictation fields are encounter ID, concerns, options actually explained, client preference and agreed next step; the psychologist is their producer. Missing or ambiguous content is manually entered in s2; no model infers unspoken findings.
Try native {OTHER} note templates and plain dictation before a summarizing loop. The 18% note share and 60% remaining are provisional model estimates, not measured facts.
Restrict the clinical data processor and recording retention through the organization's access and privacy review.
unknowns: Whether plain dictation is already used
research_questions: Does a summarizing draft outperform plain dictation after clinical correction time?

already_counted.description: Post-session capture, semantic review and correction of the note

incremental.description: Audit draft omissions and record-interface failures

approvals.approved_version: Corrected advice note accepted at the end of s2, including all clinical edits; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High:7.2 note-writing hours saved less one audit hour, below central net6.2. Low: dictation and correction consume most drafting gains. Clinical-record commitment and counseling retain full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Coordinate and evaluate staff and interns delivering patient assessment and treatment.

steps.what: Review caseloads, treatment records and staff progress before allocating supervision
Discuss cases, assign responsibilities and evaluate the quality of clinical work
Prepare the agreed action and responsibility record
Verify and commit the final staff responsibilities and review dates

tasks.design: Configure a restricted supervisor action form in {PROJECT}, using staff and case references rather than duplicating clinical records. The psychologist enters decisions once, checks the final responsibilities and review dates, and commits them; evaluation and discussion stay human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Freeform meeting records repeat assignment headings and staff identifiers.
tasks.enabler_now: Native structured action forms can replace repeated formatting without interpreting staff performance.
tasks.still_hard: Detecting weak clinical judgement and balancing workload against patient risk.
tasks.human_edge: Decide when staff need direct supervision and give difficult feedback.

ambition.what: Review overdue supervision actions at the weekly clinical coordination meeting.

tasks.altitude: Less formatting of actions; the same responsibility for staff evaluation and patient safeguards.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: structured action forms can reuse identifiers and review-date fields without automating staff evaluation.

assumptions: Boundary is clinical team direction and evaluation, including recording agreed responsibilities. It excludes the separate teaching session in task 22192.

Existing caseload and progress records are produced by treating clinicians. s2 creates directions and findings; s3 manually captures action text, owner, case reference and review date. Missing identifiers are entered manually, not inferred.
First configure a native restricted form in {PROJECT}; only formatting and repeated identifier entry in s3 shrink. Reading cases, discussion and final verification keep full time.
Only focal supervisor work is in the denominator. Staff discussion and clinical documentation are unchanged outside work, with no transfer or added capture.
The record is a supervisor work list, not automated employee scoring. National consultation requirements and access to personnel information are checked before rollout.
unknowns: Whether this action form already exists
research_questions: Can the action form eliminate duplicate formatting without adding supervisor data entry?

incremental.description: Review supervisor-form access and action-field relevance

approvals.approved_version: Completed staff action draft checked against s2 decisions immediately before committing the same revision

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central net 3.5%: 4 hours less repeated action formatting, less 0.5 upkeep. Low assumes actions are mostly novel narrative and the form saves only its upkeep. No staff assessment time is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise and teach interns, trainee clinicians and counselors.

steps.what: Select case material and training exercises for the trainee's learning goals
Observe practice, discuss formulations and coach the trainee through clinical decisions
Enter session feedback and next learning objectives into the supervision log
Check and attest the final supervision log

tasks.design: Use approved resource bundles in {LMS} linked to {DOCS}, selected by learning objective rather than generated clinical cases. Reuse the session and trainee identifiers in a supervision log, while the psychologist writes feedback, checks the final assessment and attests it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Teaching resources and supervision logs require separate preparation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native learning-objective tags and log forms can reuse existing approved content.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding why a trainee made an unsafe decision and giving useful feedback.
tasks.human_edge: Model clinical reasoning and assess readiness for greater independence.

ambition.what: Provide a focused formulation refresher for counselors changing clinical specialties.

tasks.altitude: Reinvest small preparation savings in targeted coaching; no new competence certification rights.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: tagged approved resources and native log forms can reduce preparation and repeated identifiers; supervision is still clinical judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is a teaching and supervision session with its learning log; team allocation records in task 22185 are distinct and not counted here.
Training lead maintains resource ID, version, objective tag and approval status. s1 selects and adapts resources; missing objectives require manual preparation within its remaining time.
s2 produces feedback and observed competence. s3 records trainee ID, session date, objectives, feedback and next objective. Only identifiers and headings are prefilled; judgement text stays manual.
Try native {LMS} resource bundles and log forms first. No patient encounter is recorded or sent to a model. Trainee participation is unchanged outside labour.
Estimated shares need measurement; already configured resource bundles earn no new saving.
research_questions: Do reused resources still fit each trainee's clinical learning gap?

incremental.description: Retire outdated teaching resources and check objective tags

approvals.approved_version: Final feedback and assessment in the s3 supervision log checked immediately before attestation; edits require a new attestation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central net 5.5%: 4.5 preparation and 1.75 repeated-entry hours removed, less 0.75 upkeep. Low assumes almost all resources need substantial adaptation. All coaching and attestation time remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose appropriate outside care and refer the client safely.

steps.what: Assess referral need from the client's condition and existing clinical record
Discuss referral options and obtain the client's disclosure agreement
Confirm the receiving service's remit, contact details and referral requirements
Prepare the referral letter and record the permitted disclosure scope

loop.input: Clinician-selected record passages, manually entered referral purpose, verified destination and permitted disclosure scope
loop.output: Referral draft with each clinical statement linked to selected evidence
loop.check: Psychologist checks relevance, chronology, risk statements and omission of information outside the agreed disclosure scope
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; missing source or recipient requirements causes manual letter preparation
loop.why_not_simpler: Clinical history needs selective narrative summarization. Native templates fill headings and identifiers but cannot select and phrase relevant history.

steps.what: Review the final referral, recipient and disclosure scope and authorize sending
Refer clients to specialists or support services through the secure clinical exchange

tasks.design: First use the native referral form and secure exchange in the clinical record category of {OTHER}. Add a bounded summary draft only for narrative history, with manually captured indication and disclosure scope; send the final package only after the psychologist approves its content and verified recipient.
tasks.previous_blocker: Referral letters need selective summaries from long clinical records and careful disclosure limits.
tasks.enabler_now: Record templates handle fixed fields while a bounded model can propose a sourced narrative.
tasks.still_hard: Selecting appropriate care and confirming capacity or eligibility with the receiving service.
tasks.human_edge: Balance clinical need, client preference and confidentiality.
tasks.altitude: Spend less time composing letters, with the same referral and disclosure decisions.

reach.learn: Minimum necessary disclosure and exchange receipts

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a bounded model can draft a selected clinical history, but referral selection and disclosure approval require a clinician.

assumptions: Boundary ends at sending the referral; recipient triage and acceptance are outside and unchanged. No recipient labour saving is claimed.

Clinical record entries are existing treating-clinician work. s4 includes manual selection of source passages and capture of purpose, client ID, destination ID, disclosure scope, agreement date and recipient contact. Missing or ambiguous fields require manual preparation.
s3 verifies recipient remit and contact from the maintained service directory or by manual contact; the model does not invent service availability.
Test the native referral template and secure exchange first; only residual narrative drafting uses a loop. All shares and savings are unmeasured estimates.
s5 approval binds the final letter, attachments, recipient and disclosure scope. Any edit requires fresh approval; urgent care is handled through existing human procedures, not this draft queue.
unknowns: Availability of a maintained destination directory
research_questions: Does source selection and correction still leave useful narrative drafting savings?

already_counted.description: Source selection, disclosure capture and draft correction

incremental.description: Audit referral omissions and secure-exchange failures

approvals.approved_version: Final letter, attachments, destination and disclosure scope snapshot approved in s5; changes invalidate the send authorization

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central net 18%: 15 drafting hours and 5 sending hours saved, less 2 upkeep. Low assumes all letters require manual drafting but approved exchange removes 5 dispatch hours. Referral judgement and client discussion keep full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep clinical advice and supervision human while reducing clinical note and referral preparation.
role.ambitious_version: More targeted trainee support with clear, clinician-approved records and referrals.
